### Methods
Call the "moving average" function so that we can create moving window averages for the stream chemistry data.

Clean the data files by selecting only the relevant columns and adding a "site" column to keep track of sites once the data files are merged.

Call the "moving_average" function on each dataset.

Merge the moving_average output files into one larger data frame.  Pivot to create "nutrient" and "concentration" columns.

### Results
Plot the new data.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
clean_comb_piv <- read_csv("../output/clean_combine_pivot.csv")
ggplot(
  data = clean_comb_piv,
  mapping = aes(
    x = window_start,
    y = concentration,
    linetype = Site
  )
) + geom_line()+
  facet_wrap(
    vars(nutrient), 
    scales = "free", 
    ncol = 1
  )+
  geom_vline(xintercept = ymd("1989-09-17"), linetype = "dashed")
```

This graph shows nutrient concentrations over time in the four stream sites between 1986 and 1995.  The figure contains one plot for each nutrient (Ca, Mg, K, NH4-N, and NO3-N).  Line types denote different sites.
